primitives.name: Team Lineup Decision
primitives.verbatim_quote: Abstract: Dilemma is to decide whether a player should be in-team for a certain match or not.
primitives.assumptions: Players are modeled as independent stochastic variables with measurable performance metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When O is unknown or undefined, L becomes non-deterministic.

layer2.mapping: L = f(P_1, ..., P_n; O) where f is a learned ensemble function from historical data.
layer2.telemetry: Match outcome accuracy and lineup selection consistency

primitives.name: Performance Indicator Profile
primitives.verbatim_quote: Performance indicators are defined as the variables that elucidate some aspects of performance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_k': 'Indicator k (dimensionless)', 'F_i': 'Form of player i (dimensionless)', 'A_i': 'Agility of player i (m/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each I_k contributes independently to overall team performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When I_k is undefined or zero, contribution to performance is negligible.

layer2.mapping: I_k ≅ g(F_i, A_i, H_i, ...) where g is a composite scoring function.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between I_k and match outcomes

primitives.name: Predictive Team Formation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This system helps predict a better team formation according to the geographical, performance factors.
primitives.assumptions: Formation T_f maximizes expected utility under constraints of G_f and P_f.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When G_f or P_f are inconsistent, T_f becomes suboptimal.

layer2.mapping: T_f = argmax U(G_f, P_f) subject to constraint set C.
layer2.telemetry: Expected win rate given T_f and environmental inputs

The core problem addressed is team lineup selection under uncertainty. The primitive 'team_lineup_decision' formalizes this as a conditional assignment problem where each player's inclusion depends on opponent strength and their own performance indicators. These indicators are aggregated into a structured profile through 'performance_indicator_profile', which maps raw statistics to interpretable metrics. The predictive mechanism 'predictive_team_formation' then uses these profiles to generate optimal formations based on environmental and performance factors. The mathematical duality lies in treating both individual player contributions and collective team dynamics as functions of shared latent variables. Failure modes include overfitting due to insufficient data, misalignment between indicator weights and actual game impact, and breakdown when opponent data is unavailable. The system assumes independence among players and linearity in indicator influence, which may not hold in complex tactical scenarios.
